title: Perturbed worms adopt the anterior stem-cell distribution of the species they resemble

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Perturbed worms adopt the anterior stem-cell distribution of the species they resemble

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In octanol-treated G. dorotocephala regenerates, the transformation toward another species' head shape extends to the species-characteristic distribution of neoblasts (mitotic stem cells) in the anterior body, and the authors conclude that the patterning processes disrupted by gap junction perturbation also organize the distribution of mitotically active cells.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.5. Distribution of Neoblasts Is Altered to That of Other Species in GJ-Perturbed Worms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We conclude that the transformation of G. dorotocephala worms to resemble other species also extends to the species-specific, characteristic internal distribution of their stem cells, and that the patterning processes that are disrupted after GJC perturbation are also responsible for organizing the distribution of mitotically active cells.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “2. Results › 2.5. Distribution of Neoblasts Is Altered to That of Other Species in GJ-Perturbed Worms”. Scope: Phospho-histone H3-positive neoblasts in the anterior sixth of octanol-treated G. dorotocephala and wild-type G. dorotocephala, D. japonica and S. mediterranea

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The species-characteristic distribution is measurable from existing published staining. The broader conclusion about the responsible patterning process remains confounded and needs more direct perturbation evidence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count phospho-histone-H3-positive cells in the anterior sixth under blinded labels and compare pseudo groups with wild-type species distributions. The mechanistic extension would require showing that gap-junction disruption, rather than a correlated process, controls the distribution.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The experiment establishes association more strongly than mechanism.

Per-animal counts and raw microscopy files are not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Anterior mitotic pattern is measurable, and PlanMine documents planarian stem-cell markers in general. It does not contain this octanol-treated spatial series. The further conclusion that gap-junction-sensitive patterning organizes the stem cells needs paired shape and count data that are not public.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count phospho-histone H3-positive cells in the anterior sixth and compare their spatial distribution across induced head classes and wild-type reference species. A shift of the induced animals toward the reference species' pattern would support co-transformation; no class-linked shift would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The paper's anterior mitotic counts and positions are not deposited.

Head shape and neoblast distribution can share downstream causes, so a matching distribution does not show that the same patterning process organizes both.
